task_summary: Implement a FastAPI backend API for a task management service with CRUD endpoints, health check, and psycopg2 connection pooling against PostgreSQL. The component must be fully type-annotated, tested with pytest, and kept under 300 lines per file.

findings.topic: FastAPI project structure for 300-line file limit
findings.finding: Standard FastAPI layered architecture separates concerns into: (1) main.py — app factory, lifespan, middleware; (2) routes/tasks.py — APIRouter with endpoint handlers; (3) models.py — Pydantic models and enums; (4) db.py — connection pool management and raw SQL query functions. This four-file split naturally keeps each file well under 300 lines for a CRUD service of this scope.
findings.relevance: Directly satisfies the 300-line file limit preference while maintaining clean separation of concerns

findings.finding: Use psycopg2.pool.ThreadedConnectionPool (not SimpleConnectionPool) since FastAPI runs on a threaded server (uvicorn with thread pool executor for sync endpoints). Initialize the pool in a FastAPI lifespan context manager and close it on shutdown. Always use try/finally or context managers to return connections via pool.putconn(conn). Set minconn=1, maxconn=10 as sensible defaults. Mark connections with conn.autocommit or use explicit commit/rollback in finally blocks to avoid leaving transactions open.
findings.relevance: Core infrastructure requirement — connection leaks and pool exhaustion are the #1 production issue with psycopg2 pooling

findings.finding: FastAPI's @asynccontextmanager lifespan replaces deprecated on_event('startup')/on_event('shutdown'). The lifespan function should read DATABASE_URL from os.environ (with fallback), call init_connection_pool before yield, and call close_connection_pool after yield. This ensures deterministic cleanup.
findings.relevance: Ensures pool is initialized before requests and torn down cleanly; aligns with modern FastAPI idioms

findings.topic: Pydantic v2 model design for task CRUD
findings.finding: Use Pydantic v2 (pydantic>=2.0) BaseModel with model_config. TaskStatus should be a StrEnum (Python 3.11+) so it serializes naturally to JSON strings. TaskCreateRequest should have title: str (with min_length=1, max_length=255) and optional description. TaskUpdateRequest should have all fields Optional to support partial updates. TaskResponse should include id (UUID as str), title, description, status, created_at, updated_at (ISO 8601 strings). Use Annotated types for reusable constraints (e.g., TaskTitle = Annotated[str, Field(min_length=1, max_length=255)]).
findings.source: Pydantic v2 docs, FastAPI Pydantic integration guide
findings.relevance: Type definitions are central to the contract; proper validation prevents bad data reaching the DB layer

findings.topic: UUID primary keys and SQL schema
findings.finding: Use UUID v4 for task IDs generated server-side (uuid.uuid4()). In PostgreSQL, use the uuid type natively. Store timestamps as TIMESTAMPTZ with DEFAULT NOW(). Use a db migration or an init SQL block to CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS. This avoids integer ID enumeration attacks and simplifies distributed systems.
findings.source: PostgreSQL documentation, OWASP API security guidelines
findings.relevance: TaskId is typed as a primitive (string) — UUID strings are the standard approach for REST APIs

findings.finding: Always use parameterized queries (cursor.execute('SELECT ... WHERE id = %s', (task_id,))). Never use f-strings or .format() for SQL. For dynamic UPDATE SET clauses (partial updates), build the SET clause programmatically from validated field names using a whitelist, and pass values as parameters. Use psycopg2.sql module for dynamic identifier composition if needed.
findings.source: psycopg2 docs, OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
findings.relevance: Critical security requirement — db_update_task with dynamic fields dict is the highest-risk function

findings.finding: Raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=...) for not-found tasks. Use a custom exception handler for database errors to return 500 with ErrorDetail schema. For validation errors, FastAPI auto-returns 422 with RequestValidationError. Add explicit handlers for psycopg2.Error to avoid leaking stack traces. Return ErrorDetail/ValidationErrorResponse from these handlers to match the defined types.
findings.relevance: The spec includes ErrorDetail and ValidationErrorResponse types — these must map to actual error responses

findings.topic: pytest testing strategy for FastAPI + psycopg2
findings.finding: Use two test layers: (1) Unit/integration tests using FastAPI TestClient (from httpx) — these test routes, serialization, and validation without a real DB by mocking the db module. (2) Contract tests that connect to a real PostgreSQL via DATABASE_URL env var, testing db_* functions directly. Use pytest fixtures with transaction rollback (BEGIN at setup, ROLLBACK at teardown) to keep contract tests isolated and idempotent. Use @pytest.mark.skipif(not os.environ.get('DATABASE_URL')) to skip contract tests when no DB is available.
findings.source: pytest docs, FastAPI testing guide, contract testing patterns
findings.relevance: Operating procedures mandate all functions have tests and contract tests connect via DATABASE_URL

findings.topic: Concurrency considerations: sync psycopg2 in async FastAPI
findings.finding: psycopg2 is synchronous. FastAPI will run sync endpoint functions in a thread pool automatically (def, not async def). However, defining endpoints as `def` (not `async def`) is the correct approach when using synchronous DB drivers — FastAPI dispatches them to a threadpool. Do NOT use async def with synchronous psycopg2 calls as it will block the event loop. Alternatively, use run_in_executor explicitly if endpoints must be async.
findings.source: FastAPI async documentation, Starlette concurrency model
findings.relevance: Incorrect async/sync mixing is the most common performance pitfall with sync DB drivers in FastAPI

findings.finding: Health check should verify both app liveness and DB connectivity. Execute a lightweight query (SELECT 1) inside a try/except. Return {status: 'healthy', database: 'connected'} on success, or {status: 'degraded', database: 'disconnected'} with HTTP 200 (for liveness probes) or 503 (for readiness probes). Keep it fast — use a short statement_timeout.
findings.source: Kubernetes health check patterns, 12-factor app methodology
findings.relevance: health_check() is a defined function; should verify the psycopg2 pool is functional

findings.finding: For TaskUpdateRequest with all-Optional fields, distinguish between 'field not provided' (exclude from UPDATE) and 'field explicitly set to null'. Use model.model_dump(exclude_unset=True) in Pydantic v2 to get only the fields the client actually sent. Validate that at least one field is provided (reject empty updates). Whitelist allowed column names when building dynamic SQL.
findings.source: Pydantic v2 docs, REST API partial update patterns
findings.relevance: db_update_task(task_id, fields) takes a dict — the fields dict construction must handle partial updates correctly

findings.finding: Use psycopg2.extras.RealDictCursor to get query results as dicts directly, avoiding index-based column access. This aligns with the db_* function signatures that return dict types. Set cursor_factory=RealDictCursor at the connection or cursor level.
findings.relevance: All db_* functions return dict — RealDictCursor eliminates manual row-to-dict mapping

recommended_approach:
Implement the backend as four files plus two test files:

**Source files:**
1. `models.py` (~80 lines) — All Pydantic v2 models and enums: TaskStatus (StrEnum: pending, in_progress, completed), TaskCreateRequest, TaskUpdateRequest, TaskResponse, TaskListResponse, HealthResponse, DeleteConfirmation, ErrorDetail, ValidationErrorResponse. Use Annotated types for TaskTitle, TaskId, etc.

2. `db.py` (~120 lines) — psycopg2.pool.ThreadedConnectionPool management: init_connection_pool(), close_connection_pool(), get_connection() as a context manager (try/finally putconn). All db_* functions using parameterized queries and RealDictCursor. Dynamic UPDATE builder for db_update_task with column whitelist.

3. `routes.py` (~100 lines) — APIRouter with all six endpoints as sync `def` functions (not async). Map db results to Pydantic models. Raise HTTPException(404) when db_get_task returns None. Use model_dump(exclude_unset=True) for partial updates.

4. `main.py` (~50 lines) — App factory with lifespan context manager reading DATABASE_URL from env. Mount router. Register exception handlers for psycopg2.Error → 500 responses.

**Test files:**
5. `test_routes.py` (~150 lines) — Unit tests using FastAPI TestClient with mocked db module. Covers all six endpoints including validation errors, 404s, and happy paths.

6. `test_db.py` (~120 lines) — Contract tests marked with pytest.mark.skipif for DATABASE_URL absence. Tests each db_* function against real PostgreSQL with transaction-rollback fixture for isolation.

Key decisions:
- Sync endpoints (def, not async def) to avoid blocking the event loop with psycopg2
- ThreadedConnectionPool for thread safety
- UUID v4 for task IDs, generated in db_create_task
- Parameterized queries everywhere; whitelist-based dynamic SQL in db_update_task
- CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in init_connection_pool for self-bootstrapping
alternatives_considered: psycopg3 (async-native) instead of psycopg2 — rejected because the spec explicitly requires psycopg2
SQLAlchemy ORM over raw psycopg2 — rejected; spec mandates psycopg2 directly and the CRUD scope doesn't warrant ORM overhead
async def endpoints with run_in_executor wrapping — adds complexity for no gain; FastAPI auto-dispatches sync def to threadpool already
SimpleConnectionPool instead of ThreadedConnectionPool — rejected; FastAPI's threadpool executor means concurrent threads access the pool
Integer auto-increment IDs instead of UUIDs — rejected; UUID is safer for REST APIs (no enumeration) and aligns with TaskId being a string primitive
Alembic for migrations — overkill for a single-table service; CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is sufficient
risks: Connection pool exhaustion under load if get_connection callers fail to return connections — mitigated by implementing get_connection as a context manager with finally-based putconn
SQL injection in db_update_task dynamic field building — mitigated by strict whitelist of allowed column names (title, description, status) and parameterized values
Stale connections in the pool after PostgreSQL restarts — mitigated by wrapping queries in try/except for psycopg2.OperationalError and using pool with keepalive or connection testing
Contract tests may fail in CI without PostgreSQL — mitigated by skipif guard on DATABASE_URL; documented in operating procedures
Race conditions on concurrent updates to the same task — acceptable for this scope; could add optimistic locking (version column) later if needed
File exceeding 300 lines if error handling grows — mitigated by the four-file split which gives ample headroom
compliance_notes: All public functions will have type annotations per the Standards section
Composition over inheritance: models use composition (Pydantic BaseModel, not deep inheritance chains); db module is a set of functions, not a class hierarchy
Every backend function will have at least one test (unit or contract)
Contract tests will read DATABASE_URL from environment as specified
No file will exceed 300 lines — the four-source + two-test split ensures this
Python 3.12+ features available: StrEnum (3.11+), Annotated types, modern type union syntax (X | None)
